authority: Explicit user direction on 2026-10-23; applies to the intended whole character system
status: Binding architecture; user broadly accepts form, current candidate strict source fidelity remains pending

threeElements.functions: Shared mother system: continuous surfaces, anatomical relationships, deformation, expression, motion, attachment and material response are evaluated by mathematical functions.
threeElements.variables: A person is an instance of the shared functions with different parameters. Identity, proportions, feature shape, skin properties, variation seeds, pose, expression, time and state are variables, rather than a separately authored character mesh or image set.
threeElements.noise: Procedural multiscale variation supplies surface texture, grain and material variation, controlled by variables and constrained by the anatomical/material functions.

conceptualEvaluation: Person = MotherFunctions(position or chart coordinates, personVariables, proceduralNoise(coordinates, seed), time/state)

shapeAndRendering.authoritativeShape: Continuous parameterized or implicit surface functions and their variables
shapeAndRendering.surfaceVisibility: Direct numerical ray/surface intersection; do not convert the character surface into triangle or quad tessellation as the final rendering route
shapeAndRendering.noClosedFormPromise: Numerical iteration and tolerances are compatible with mathematical functions; do not promise exact closed-form intersections for the whole character.
shapeAndRendering.engineBoundary: Display-engine scheduling, screen-sized dispatch carriers, temporary acceleration bounds and caches are implementation mechanisms. They must not become an authoritative polygonal character shape.

materialAndNoise.generation: Pigment variation, skin grain, pores, roughness/oil variation and related surface qualities are procedural function/noise evaluations with parameters, rather than character-specific imported image textures.
materialAndNoise.anatomicalConstraint: Noise does not replace skull, facial features, ears, cavities or larger anatomical structure. Their shape and relationships belong to the mother functions and variables.
materialAndNoise.separateResponses: Pigment, geometric relief, roughness/oil and scattering retain separate function/variable responsibilities.
materialAndNoise.stability: Use deterministic seeds and stable surface/material coordinates so variation remains attached during pose and expression changes.
materialAndNoise.currentLimitations: Analytical shading direction only; no microdisplaced silhouette or self-occlusion; Screen-space approximation; not full volumetric/random-walk scattering

fittingAndMigration.offlineReference: Existing models and images may be inspected or sampled as reconstruction references under the user's earlier instruction.
fittingAndMigration.fittedVariables: Spline coefficients and other genuine surface-function parameters can be variables; their source derivation remains recorded.
fittingAndMigration.noDisguisedMesh: Do not relabel inherited per-vertex XYZ arrays and face connectivity as variables and claim this completes the function-only architecture.
fittingAndMigration.controlPreservation: Preserve current parameter values, meanings and observable effects during migration; no silent loss of saved adjustments.
fittingAndMigration.quality: Function/noise/variable structure does not itself certify matching shape, realistic appearance, stable intersections or acceptable speed. Verify each with real rendering.
fittingAndMigration.noAutonomousApproximation: No unapproved simplification, smoothing, layer merging, thickening, hole filling, guessed primitive substitution, structure deletion or tolerance relaxation. Reproduce source one for one first; only then apply person parameter logic.
fittingAndMigration.acceptanceOrder: Freeze source and state; preserve layered surface and boundaries; express functions from source data; validate positions, normals, curvature and first-hit visibility in matched views; then enable parameter variation.

scopeOfThisWindow: Head reconstruction; body work remains assigned to the other window
supersedes: The earlier HEAD-PLAN.json proposal to generate disposable display tessellation from the character surface
